clauses.mechanism: express revocation by EO 12553 (listed by number in its table; effective on signing, no effective-date wording)
clauses.reason: whole: EO 11771 (signed 1974-03-18, 39 FR 10415) extends to the Liaison Office of the People's Republic of China in Washington, D.C. and its duly notified members the privileges and immunities of diplomatic missions, under the act of April 20, 1973 (Public Law 93-22), with the sentence "T his Executive Order shall be effective as of" followed on the next line by the date April 20, 1973. The order has no sunset or condition of its own. First end: EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25): "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" followed by a two-column 'No. Subject' table; the entry at offset 26383 of the held EO_12553.txt reads "11771 Extending diplomatic privileges and immunities to the Liaison Office of the People’s Republic of China", which matches this order's number and subject. EO 12553 has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1986-02-25. The Office of the Federal Register catalog note reads "Revoked by: EO 12553, February 25, 1986". Held U.S. Code editorial note (release point 119-121): "Ex. Ord. No. 11771, Mar. 18, 1974, 39 F.R. 10415, which extended diplomatic privileges and immunities to the Liaison Office of the People’s Republic of China in Washington, D.C., was revoked by Ex. Ord. No. 12553, Feb. 25, 1986, 51 F.R. 7237." (22 note to 22 U.S.C. 288i)
